knowledgeAnswers.rationale: Isolating the pump first stops debris being drawn into it, and checking freeboard and the overflow route confirms the pond will not overtop.
Edge stones can shift or expose the liner, or let soil wash in, so they are checked and recorded at each visit.
Root damage near the liner is recorded and referred; cutting roots near the liner can cause leaks.

practicalCriteria: Learner completes procedure step 1: Confirm the access route and any parts the owner has asked you to keep clear.
Learner completes procedure step 2: Isolate the pump before clearing any blockage at the outlet, the intake or the overflow, and prove it off.
Learner completes procedure step 3: Check the outlet screen, the inlet return and the overflow route, and record any blockage or movement.
Learner completes procedure step 4: Measure freeboard and water depth at the fixed reference point, and record sediment depth at the same point.
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Record of procedure step 1: Confirm the access route and any parts the owner has asked you to keep clear.
Record of procedure step 3: Check the outlet screen, the inlet return and the overflow route, and record any blockage or movement.
Record of procedure step 4: Measure freeboard and water depth at the fixed reference point, and record sediment depth at the same point.
stopWorkCriteria: Stop work if procedure step 2 is not done: Isolate the pump before clearing any blockage at the outlet, the intake or the overflow, and prove it off.
Stop work if procedure step 4 is not done: Measure freeboard and water depth at the fixed reference point, and record sediment depth at the same point.
Stop work if procedure step 5 is not done: Inspect edge stones, slabs and pavers for movement, soil wash-in and exposed liner, and make the area safe before working on any bank.
